accepted.sentence: With air-independent propulsion, some non-nuclear vessels can remain underwater longer without running diesel engines or raising an air intake.
During brief surface intervals, exposed satellite-navigation antennas can obtain position fixes that correct accumulated errors in inertial estimates.
During shipyard overhauls, a dry dock supports the hull above water, letting workers inspect and repair normally immersed surfaces.
In heavy seas, traveling below the wave zone avoids much surface motion, though currents can still alter a vessel’s track.
When radio contact is unavailable, nearby vessels can exchange short, low-rate messages through acoustic communication in the surrounding water.
On extended patrols, food supplies often set the maximum deployment length, even when the propulsion system could operate longer.
After surfacing, crews may use radar to locate nearby ships and aircraft, since radio-frequency sensing does not work through seawater.
In narrow straits with strong tidal flow, navigators compensate for water movement that can push a vessel away from its intended course.
